Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.

Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.

This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation
Ravie LakshmananOct 15, 2026Vulnerability / Network Security
Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday issued security updates for a high-severity flaw in PAN-OS software that has come under active exploitation.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of remote code execution in the management interface.
"A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall," Palo Alto Networks said.
The issue impacts PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series). Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected by the vulnerability.
Palo Alto Networks said that no special configuration is required to exploit the issue, but said the security risk can be minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses.
"You can reduce the risk of exploitation by restricting access to a jump box that is the only system allowed to access the management interface," it said.
Patches are available in the following versions -
PAN-OS >= 12.1.4-h12, >= 12.1.7-h8, >= 12.1.10-h2
PAN-OS >= 11.2.4-h22, >= 11.2.7-h21, >= 11.2.10-h15, >= 11.2.13-h3, >= 11.2.16 (ETA: October 15, 2026)
PAN-OS >= 11.1.4-h37, >= 11.1.6-h39, >= 11.1.7-h11, >= 11.1.10-h35, >= 11.1.13-h15, >= 11.1.16-h3
PAN-OS >= 10.2.7-h38, >= 10.2.10-h41, >= 10.2.13-h26, >= 10.2.16-h11, >= 10.2.18-h12
The network security company also acknowledged it has seen "very limited exploitation" targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface, but did not elaborate on the nature of the malicious activity involved, who is behind the effort, or when it began.
The following IP addresses geolocated to the U.S. are assessed to be linked to the exploit attempts -
It credited Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks, with discovering and reporting the vulnerability.
The disclosure comes as Cisco warned that threat actors are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76519, CVSS score: 9.8) that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.
"This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled," it said. "An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system."
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has since added both CVE-2026-0322 and CVE-2026-76519 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to prioritize fixes by October 17, 2026.

Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices.
Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks.
"Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said.
The vulnerability has a severity score of 8.6 and affects PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, as well as Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances. Palo Alto says Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.
To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface.
Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only.
The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.
Customers running older, unsupported versions must upgrade to a supported release.
Palo Alto says there are no known workarounds for the vulnerability, but customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can enable signatures that provide limited protection against known attack patterns.
"Limited coverage in Threat Prevention means that while known attack patterns can be identified using the current Threat ID, variations may exist that cannot currently be detected," warns Palo Alto.
"If this CVE and Required Configuration for Exposure impact your environment, we recommend upgrading to an unaffected version."
The vulnerability was discovered internally by Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks.
The company also shared three IP addresses that have been exploiting the flaw: 66.42.72[.]14, 208.83.239[.]114, and 149.248.47[.]234.
BleepingComputer contacted Palo Alto Networks to learn when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks, and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to access internal networks.
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has now added CVE-2026-0322 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requires federal civilian agencies to mitigate the vulnerability by October 17.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) Pays a Large Part of Its Wage Bill in Stock. What Does That Do to Profit?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:49 AM CDT 4 min read
Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW) closed at $346.95 on October 19. The stock has returned 104.62% over the last 6 months, compared to an 11.6% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 8.7% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.
Palo Alto Networks sells security software to large companies, and by most measures it is doing well. Revenue rose 34.50% in its most recent quarter, and the shares have doubled in six months. The reported profit does not look like any of that. The company earned $307 million on revenue of $11.48 billion, and much of the explanation sits in how it pays its staff.

Palo Alto (PANW) Pays a Large Part of Its Wage Bill in Stock. What Does That Do to Profit?
Why the Cash Looks Nothing Like the Profit:
Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.
Strip it out and the business looks entirely different. Operating cash flow reached $4.55 billion across the same year, more than fourteen times the reported profit, and borrowing is negligible at 9.34% of equity.
Palo Alto is one of the ten in our 10 Most Promising Cloud Stocks According to Hedge Funds. To see which companies rank above it, click HERE.
Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.

Which Number the Price Is Using:
The stock changes hands at 94.34 times what analysts expect next year. That multiple is built on earnings measured after adding the share-based cost back, not on the profit the company actually reported.
So the price depends on which definition a buyer accepts. On the reported figure, the stock is extraordinarily expensive, and on the adjusted one it is merely expensive. Security budgets have been growing quickly. 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy in 2026 has the names competing for them.
Conclusion:
This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. That cost falls on owners through dilution rather than on the company through cash, and the tax line closed what was left. Watch the share count rather than the earnings line, because that is where this particular cost is actually recorded.

Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday issued security updates for a high-severity flaw in PAN-OS software that has come under active exploitation.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of remote code execution in the management interface.
"A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall," Palo Alto Networks said.
The issue impacts PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series). Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected by the vulnerability.
Palo Alto Networks said that no special configuration is required to exploit the issue, but said the security risk can be minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses.
"You can reduce the risk of exploitation by restricting access to a jump box that is the only system allowed to access the management interface," it said.
Patches are available in the following versions -
PAN-OS >= 12.1.4-h12, >= 12.1.7-h8, >= 12.1.10-h2
PAN-OS >= 11.2.4-h22, >= 11.2.7-h21, >= 11.2.10-h15, >= 11.2.13-h3, >= 11.2.16 (ETA: October 15, 2026)
PAN-OS >= 11.1.4-h37, >= 11.1.6-h39, >= 11.1.7-h11, >= 11.1.10-h35, >= 11.1.13-h15, >= 11.1.16-h3
PAN-OS >= 10.2.7-h38, >= 10.2.10-h41, >= 10.2.13-h26, >= 10.2.16-h11, >= 10.2.18-h12
The network security company also acknowledged it has seen "very limited exploitation" targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface, but did not elaborate on the nature of the malicious activity involved, who is behind the effort, or when it began.

It credited Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks, with discovering and reporting the vulnerability.
The disclosure comes as Cisco warned that threat actors are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76519, CVSS score: 9.8) that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.
"This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled," it said. "An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system."
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has since added both CVE-2026-0322 and CVE-2026-76519 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to prioritize fixes by October 17, 2026.

Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices.
Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks.
"Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said.
The vulnerability has a severity score of 8.6 and affects PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, as well as Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances. Palo Alto says Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.
To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface.
Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only.
The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.
Customers running older, unsupported versions must upgrade to a supported release.
Palo Alto says there are no known workarounds for the vulnerability, but customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can enable signatures that provide limited protection against known attack patterns.
"Limited coverage in Threat Prevention means that while known attack patterns can be identified using the current Threat ID, variations may exist that cannot currently be detected," warns Palo Alto.
"If this CVE and Required Configuration for Exposure impact your environment, we recommend upgrading to an unaffected version."
The vulnerability was discovered internally by Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks.
The company also shared three IP addresses that have been exploiting the flaw: 66.42.72[.]14, 208.83.239[.]114, and 149.248.47[.]234.
BleepingComputer contacted Palo Alto Networks to learn when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks, and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to access internal networks.
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has now added CVE-2026-0322 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requires federal civilian agencies to mitigate the vulnerability by October 17.

Palo Alto Networks Reports Fiscal Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 1, 2026 — Palo Alto Networks® (NASDAQ: PANW), the global AI cybersecurity leader, announced today financial results for its fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal year, ended July 31, 2026.
"We delivered a strong Q4 to close out the year, adding nearly $1 billion of Net New NGS ARR in a single quarter," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and chief executive officer of Palo Alto Networks. "The latest advancements in AI are elevating cybersecurity to the top of the CIO priority list, and will serve as durable tailwinds as we progress towards our $20 billion FY30 NGS ARR target."
"We delivered a strong finish to a record year and exceeded our guidance across the board, fueled by strength across our Network & AI Security, Cortex, and Idira platforms," said Dipak Golechha, chief financial officer of Palo Alto Networks. "Our profitable growth framework continues to scale effectively, reinforcing our confidence in achieving 40% adjusted free cash flow margin in FY28."
Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights
•Total revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 grew 34% year over year to $3.41 billion.
•Next-Generation Security ARR for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 grew 63% year over year to $9.10 billion.
•Remaining performance obligations grew 34% year over year to $21.2 billion.
•GAAP operating income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $172 million, compared with GAAP operating income of $497 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Non-GAAP operating income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.0 billion, compared with non-GAAP operating income of $768 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
•GAAP net loss for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $282 million, or ($0.35) per diluted share, compared with GAAP net income of $254 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Non-GAAP net income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $853 million, or $1.02 per diluted share, compared with non-GAAP net income of $673 million, or $0.95 per diluted share, for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
•Net cash provided by operating activities for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.4 billion, compared with net cash provided by operating activities of $1.0 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Adjusted free cash flow for fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.3 billion, compared with adjusted free cash flow of $954 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Fiscal year 2026 adjusted free cash flow margin was 38.4%. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
Palo Alto Networks has acquired Console, an AI-native platform that enables agentic workflows across enterprise operations. Console will expand the role of our Cortex platform across the broader enterprise agentic transformation.
Palo Alto Networks provides guidance based on current market conditions and expectations.
For the fiscal first quarter 2027, we expect:
•Next-Generation Security ARR of $9.54 billion to $9.56 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 63%.
•Remaining performance obligations of $20.8 billion to $20.9 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 34% to 35%.
•Total revenue in the range of $3.300 billion to $3.310 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 33% to 34%.
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $0.96 to $0.98, using 837 million to 844 million shares outstanding.
For the fiscal year 2027, we expect:
•Next-Generation Security ARR of $11.075 billion to $11.175 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 22% to 23%.
•Remaining performance obligations of $25.2 billion to $25.4 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 19% to 20%.
•Total revenue in the range of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 23% to 24%.
•Non-GAAP operating margin of 29.5%.
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $4.16 to $4.19, using 844 million to 847 million shares outstanding.
•Adjusted free cash flow margin to be 38.0%.
